findings.claim: The arroyo commit callable is invoked from the background _commit_loop thread rather than the consumer/StreamProcessor thread, so KafkaConsumer's unlocked stage_offsets/commit state is accessed concurrently with the main loop and rebalance callbacks.

verifier.reason: ResultsStrategyFactory.create_thread_queue_parallel_worker passes arroyo's commit callable via commit_offsets into SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py:244-259), which spawns a daemon thread self.commit_thread that invokes self.commit_function(committable) from _commit_loop rather than poll() on the StreamProcessor thread (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:270-287). Because arroyo's StreamProcessor and KafkaConsumer maintain unlocked offset/staging state accessed on the consumer thread during poll(), commit_offsets(), and rebalance callbacks, calling commit from the background thread causes concurrent unlocked access.
